messages.subject: Can semTools::reliability() deal with single-indicator-latents?
parts:
Hi fellow lavaan-users!

I tried to use semTools::reliability() with a CFA  that has some single-indicator-latents and i get this error:
"Error in trueitem + erritem : non-conformable arrays"

What does this mean? Is this because you can´t get reliability values for the si-latents? Is there a workaround?

Any help is appreciated! Thanks!
Niels

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can semTools::reliability() deal with single-indicator-latents?
parts:
I tried to use semTools::reliability() with a CFA  that has some single-indicator-latents and i get this error:
"Error in trueitem + erritem : non-conformable arrays"

What does this mean? Is this because you can´t get reliability values for the si-latents? Is there a workaround?

Programmatically, there is probably an issue with single-indicator constructs such that a matrix might reduce to a vector unless "drop = FALSE" is specified in brackets.  Conceptually, there is no way to estimate reliability of a test with only one item.  The formula for alpha would end up dividing by zero in the k / (k - 1) term.  The formula for AVE or omega should work out to 1 because the error variance is fixed to zero (unless you fix it to another quantity based on reliability, in which case your reliability estimate would be the same as the one you already have), so the numerator and denominator are the same quantity.  

My suggestion is to just take out the single-indicator constructs and calculate reliability among the rest.

Terry

Hi Terrance,
thank you for your answer! I had the single-indicator-error-variance fixed to a specified value, so i don´t need a reliabilty-estimate for them. But i wasn´t sure, if the model would produce different values for the others, if i leave the si out.

I followed your suggestion and took the single-indicator-items out and tried reliabilty(), then i tried my idea of using the model with single-indicator-items, but use reliabilityL2 with my first-level-latents and only look at the omegaL1-coefficient.
